summary: Kickoff to align MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs around latency and uptime, and KMS keying options for private deployments. Main blockers: procurement needs a clear pricing line for KMS-hosted HSM and egress tolerance; legal wants tighter audit log commitments and a DPA clause for deletion windows. Action items and owners captured, demo requested for KMS flow in a VPC.
transcript:
Meeting header:
2026-10-29 15:00 PDT · 1h 2m
Attendees: Sasha (Redwood AE), Marta (Redwood SE), Daniel (CS), Priya (Procurement), Derek (Legal), Imani (Security), Owen (Infra)

00:00 Sasha: ok everyone thanks for carving time, uh this is Sasha from Redwood Inference, i'll run through the agenda — MSA/DPA redline alignment, KMS keying options, the SLA and pricing handoff.
00:17 Priya: hi, thanks. quick ask — can we get a one-page summary of the commercial terms we actually need to present to finance? they need numbers not prose.
00:28 Sasha: totally, we'll include a price table. we'll also call out the KMS add-on as a separate line item — Marta will cover that.
00:35 Marta: hi all, im Marta. for KMS we support two modes: 1) customer-managed keys via bring-your-own-kms in the VPC (key material never leaves your HSM), 2) Redwood-managed envelope keys backed by our cloud KMS — cheaper but less control.
00:55 Owen: for us, the absolute requirement is HSM-backed keys with customer custody. we need to be able to rotate and revoke without Redwood retaining plaintext.
01:05 Marta: yes that's the BYOK flow. small caveat: there are operational latencies on key unwrap on cold-starts, that's like 30–150 ms per new warm-up, we can mitigate with caching.
01:20 Imani: security also wants to see how audit logs look — who touched the keys, key rotation events, and proof of deletion. we can't accept fuzzy language on deletion windows.
01:33 Derek: from legal — our main concerns with the DPA are deletion guarantees and data subject access assistance. also need liability caps tied to SLA breaches.
01:45 Sasha: understood. on deletion, Redwood offers controlled deletion workflows; we'll call out a 30-day retention/complete purge window in the DPA default, but we can discuss shorter windows for an addendum.
01:59 Priya: procurement wants to know if that 30-day purge window impacts compliance with our data-retention policies — sometimes our retention is 90 days.
02:10 Marta: the 30-day number is a default for hosted API logs; for Private deployments in your VPC, you control logs retention entirely. so if you need 90 days, that's in your control.
02:25 Owen: good, so for Cardinal's private deployment we'll manage logs and retention — Redwood won't have access to raw logs unless we grant it.
02:37 Sasha: moving to SLA: our standard is 99.9% monthly uptime for dedicated plans, with token-latency SLOs for certain latency profiles — we can map to your 95th percentile requirements.
02:50 Priya: finance needs a service credit table and a clear escalation path documented — we can't leave this vague for approval.
03:03 Sasha: we'll attach a service credit schedule to the SLA doc; typical is pro rata credits for downtime, and for persistent latency regressions we can do rollback and credits.
03:12 Derek: legal: need to see max liability on data breaches, and we want to avoid open-ended indemnities. also would like to push for SOC2 + yearly audits, and the right to audit with notice.
03:27 Daniel: on Redwood's side we can provide SOC2 report and a SOC2 letter; we do annual third-party assessments.
03:33 Imani: can you confirm whether Redwood maintains a key escrowing capability in any flow? we need to ensure no incidental escrow.
03:41 Marta: no escrow by default in BYOK. in Redwood-managed keys we hold envelope keys but not plaintext model weights, etc. we'll clarify in the security appendix.
03:55 Sasha: pricing — there's base API usage, then a Private deployment platform fee, a Dedicated GPU reserved capacity line, and the KMS HSM add-on. Priya, do you need a per-GB egress charge spelled out?
04:08 Priya: yes, please. our procurement model must include predictable egress and a variance cap for budgeting.
04:17 Sasha: we can do a tiered egress schedule with a cap — and include a surge protection discount for the first quarter of go-live.
04:28 Owen: technical note: if we keep keys in our HSM and run in our VPC, will the per-request latency be impacted if Redwood does routing? i.e., if traffic goes to Redwood region first then to our VPC to unwrap, that's bad.
04:44 Marta: for private deployments we'd colocate inference within your VPC or on-prem runtime, there's no outbound hop for key unwraps. the BYOK flow keeps key operations local.
04:55 Derek: can you add specific network egress/ingress diagrams into the security appendix, we need that for our architecture review board.
05:03 Sasha: yes we'll attach a network diagram — link to draft: https://redwood.internal/docs/kms-vpc-diagram (shared)
05:15 Imani: can we see a sample of the audit log format? JSON schema ideally.
05:22 Marta: i'll post the sample after the call, small caveat — the transcription of user ids is obfuscated in hosted by default but in private you can keep full traces.
05:33 Derek: legal — if we request an on-site audit or evidence we want to limit the burden: 30 days notice and scope limited to platform-specific controls only.
05:45 Sasha: that's reasonable. next, DPA redlines: Derek, can you summarize your top 5 asks so we can map exceptions?
05:51 Derek: sure — 1) tighter deletion commitments; 2) liability cap aligned to fees paid in the prior 12 months; 3) audit rights with notice; 4) breach notification timelines shortened to 48 hours; 5) carve-outs for aggregated, deidentified telemetry.
06:12 Sasha: good list. Derek: on breach notification, we can commit to 72 hours standard, 48 hours is a stretch but i can escalate. we do want to avoid language that requires impossible forensics immediately.
06:26 Derek: we'll mark 48 hours as preferred, 72 acceptable with a clause about investigative windows, but that depends on classification.
06:38 Priya: procurement question — we need to know the approval window from Redwood's side for price lock — what's the quote validity?
06:47 Sasha: quotes are valid for 45 days from the quote date; for enterprise bookings we can extend to 90 days with a minimal advisory.
06:55 Priya: ok that's workable.
07:02 Marta: demo ask — we can run a 30-min hands-on for KMS in your staging VPC. we'll need a service account / ephemeral creds.
07:11 Owen: we'll provide a staging subnet and service account. timeline — we prefer the week of Nov 8.
07:19 Sasha: noted. action items recap: i'll send the annotated redline and pricing worksheet; Marta will schedule the KMS demo in the staging VPC; Derek will send legal exceptions list; Imani will provide SOC2 artifacts.
07:34 Derek: one more legal ask — limitation of liability carveouts for negligence need to be clearer. we'll propose language.
07:40 Sasha: understood. final Qs?
07:45 Priya: just confirm who signs the final SOW — will Redwood accept PO + signed MSA?
07:50 Sasha: yes, standard acceptance is signed MSA plus PO or a signed SOW.
07:55 Daniel: we'll also provide an onboarding runbook and a checklist for infra handoff.
08:00 Imani: thanks. can you also include a short runbook for key compromises? we want step-by-step.
08:07 Marta: yes, incident runbook for key compromise included in the security appendix.
08:12 Sasha: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts and the redline.
08:18 Priya: thanks, bye.
08:21 Derek: thanks all.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker overlap, a few proper nouns auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'BYOK' as 'bi-yok' in a couple spots).

Referenced artifacts:
